papers.title: Integral Brauer--Manin Obstruction for Fermat Near Misses
papers.abstract: We study the integral Hasse principle for the affine surfaces given by $x^4+y^4-w^2=m^2$, where $m>1$ is odd and squarefree. We give a criterion to determine if there is an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction, which depends only on simple congruence conditions on the prime factors of $m$ modulo $8$. We use this to show that for $100\%$ of such surfaces there is no integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for integral points.

papers.title: Iterated toric descent obstruction and homogeneous spaces over geometric global fields
papers.abstract: We study torsors under tori and groups of multiplicative type together with the obstruction they define to the existence of rational points in the setting of geometric global fields. Our methods give two new arithmetic applications: the iterated toric descent obstruction coincides with the toric decent obstruction and the toric obstruction is the only obstruction to the existence of rational points for homogeneous spaces of connected linear groups with either connected or abelian geometric stabilizers. These applications generalize some known results for classical global fields, due to Borovoi, Colliot-Th\'el\`ene, and Sansuc, while exhibiting novel behaviors.

papers.title: Spectral Beurling-Selberg Approximation and Applications to Effective Motivic Chebotarev-Sato-Tate Estimates
papers.abstract: We establish a spectral Beurling-Selberg approximation theorem on compact connected Riemannian manifolds for sets whose boundaries have finite upper Minkowski content. Our majorants and minorants have controlled spectral coefficients and explicit stability under Hausdorff perturbations, uniformly over families satisfying a common Minkowski content bound. We extend the construction to singular spaces arising from Riemannian submetries with basic mean curvature, and apply it to equidistribution on quaternionic Shimura varieties. Assuming the conjectural formalism of the specified motivic L-functions, including the motivic Riemann hypothesis, we develop effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimates for fixed sets and varying families with controlled boundary geometry and Hausdorff variation, and describe how additional symmetries improve the error exponents. The proofs combine classical analytic methods with new methods from differential geometry, analytic geometry, and Riemannian spectral analysis. Applications include an asymptotic formula for a motivic analogue of Atkin-Serre estimates and tubular estimates for Picard-rank jumps of K3 surfaces via their transcendental motives.

papers.title: Four runners that are barely lonely
papers.abstract: For positive integers $v_1,\dots,v_n$ let $\mathrm{ML}(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\max_t\min_i\|v_it\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer. Kravitz asked which values below $1/n$ occur. For $n=4$, Jain and Kravitz showed that the values below $1/4$ are $m/(4m+2)$, $m\ge2$, up to finitely many undetermined exceptions. We settle the four-runner case completely. A primitive quadruple has $\mathrm{ML}<1/4$ if and only if it is, up to order, $\{1,2,3,4k\}$, or $\{x,y,x+y,x+2y\}$ with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y\not\equiv x,2x\pmod 4$, or $\{1,3,4,14\}$. The values below $1/4$ are exactly $m/(4m+2)$ with $m\ge2$, $m\ne3$, so $3/14$ is the only exception, and Conjecture 4.1 of Fan and Sun holds. A density lemma bounds the length of a quadruple on neither critical subtorus by $512$, and an exact search over 800,816,099 quadruples completes the proof. The same method shows that the two-dimensional subtori of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^4$ with loneliness below $2/5$ take exactly the three-runner values in that range, which between $1/3$ and $2/5$ are the fractions $p/q$ with $1\le 2q-5p\le 4$. Hence the accumulation points of the four-runner spectrum in $(0,2/5]$ are the three-runner values there, as Giri and Kravitz conjectured, and $9/25$ is not the loneliness of a two-dimensional subtorus. For every $n$, assuming the conjecture for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, we prove $\mathrm{ML}(v)>1/n-(n(n-1))^{n-2}/(2|v|)$, which is sharp in $|v|$, and that every $n$-tuple with $\mathrm{ML}<1/n$ and $|v|\ge n(n(n-1))^{2n-4}$ lies on a two-dimensional subtorus of loneliness $1/n$. This answers a question of Cordella. For five speeds, a two-dimensional subtorus of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^5$ with loneliness below $2/9$ is the product of a coordinate circle with the circle of $\{1,2,3,4\}$ or $\{1,3,4,7\}$. We also give infinitely many subtori whose maximizers lie off every circle with a repeated speed.

papers.title: Limit theorems for cuspidal orbits on Fuchsian groups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset \operatorname{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ be discrete, co-finite with cusps, and let ${\frak b}\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ be a cusp of $\Gamma$. Let $f: \Gamma{\frak b} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a quantum modular form in the sense that the maps $$ \phi_\gamma(x) = f(x) - f(\gamma x) \qquad (x\in \Gamma{\frak b}, \gamma \in \Gamma) $$ extend to H\"older-regular functions. Under bounded moments assumptions of the shape $\sum_n n^{-2} \int |\phi_{\gamma^n}(x)|^\alpha d x < \infty$ for some $\alpha>0$ and every fixed parabolic element $\gamma\in \Gamma$, we prove asymptotic formulas for the characteristic functions of the values $f(x)$ for $x\in \Gamma{\frak b}$, ordered by growing denominators. These yield Gaussian limits when $\alpha>2$ and other stable limit laws under suitable further assumptions. This generalizes to Fuchsian groups the work of Baladi-Vall\'ee on rational orbits of the Gauss map. In companion papers, we use this result, and in particular its flexible assumptions on $\phi_\gamma$, to deduce limit theorems for automorphic $L$-series at the central point. One ingredient in our proof is a particular cuspidal acceleration of the Bowen-Series map, whose inverse branches admit a convenient parametrization, and for which we describe explicitly a natural extension.

papers.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
papers.abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.

papers.title: A Diophantine generalization of Fourier's irrationality trick
papers.abstract: We revisit Fourier's method for proving the irrationality of $e$ and generalize it into a unified Diophantine framework, which applies to a broad class of series with bounded or mildly growing integer numerators, and suitably growing, divisible denominators. Using integer linear forms, we establish a general criterion that recovers classical irrationality results while also generating new ones within a single structural approach.

papers.title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.

papers.title: A Local Fourier-Transform Proof of Offen's Spherical Transfer Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $E/F$ be an unramified quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero and odd residual characteristic. Offen proved that, on the full spherical space of nondegenerate Hermitian matrices, equality of the Hironaka and Satake transforms implies Jacquet--Ye matching. We give a purely local proof of this theorem. The argument combines Jacquet's compatibility of matching with Fourier transform, the Godement--Jacquet functional equation, and Hironaka's scalar functional equation for Hermitian zeta integrals. The local proof recovers Jacquet's spherical-Hecke fundamental lemma from the unit case.

papers.title: Erd\H{o}s--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
papers.abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $\phi$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $\phi^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $\phi^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $\phi$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the L\'evy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: Clusters of primes revisited
papers.abstract: We revisit the generalized Rayleigh quotient optimization problem related to the Maynard-Tao sieve with the goal of finding a more efficient function basis. We demonstrate that a family based on products of reciprocals, previously used in asymptotic estimates for $H_m = \liminf_{n \to \infty}(p_{n+m}-p_n)$, provides results that are close to the theoretical limits of the sieve across many regimes. In particular, we establish $H_2 \leq 31 \, 140$, $H_3 \leq 2 \, 560 \, 022$, $H_4 \leq 193 \, 672 \, 056$, and $H_5 \leq 13 \, 659 \, 045 \, 840$. We also show that, as $k \to \infty$, the related variational quantity $M_k$, introduced by Maynard, satisfies the lower bound $M_k \geq \log k - 0.273572 + o(1)$.

papers.title: A spectral theory of zeta functions of function fields
papers.abstract: We study Hilbert spaces constructed from the Weil quadratic form associated with the zeta function of a curve over a finite field, together with self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator on these spaces. For a distinguished family of these extensions, we prove that the eigenvalues converge to the ordinates of the zeros of the zeta function and that the corresponding entire spectral functions, after normalization, converge locally uniformly to an infinite product determined by these zeros. These limits occur as the interval parameter approaches a finite endpoint, rather than infinity as in the setting of the Riemann zeta function. We also realize the global Hilbert space through the Rosati trace pairing and show that translation by $\log q$ is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by normalized Frobenius. This provides a geometric model for the analogous analytic constructions associated with the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Weil Operators and Remainders of Anderson Generating Functions over a Punctured Projective Line
papers.abstract: Let $A_\rho$ be the coordinate ring of the projective line over $\Fq$ with a closed point of degree $N$ removed. We give finite formulas for higher Weil operators in a basis of Riemann--Roch spaces, which recover the formulas of Hu--Ou--Yang when $N=1$. We identifythese operators with representatives of the residue Casimir tensors and obtain a determinant formula for the Weil pairing, relative to a chosen determinant realization. For a normalized rank-one Drinfeld module, we compute the remainder of its Anderson generating function modulo any nonconstant $p\in A_\rho$. The formula includes multiple zeros and a zero at the ordinary point at infinity. Its last coefficient is a nonzero scalar multiple of an exponential division value. When $(p)$ is a finite principal prime, a value of the associated special function at one zero of $p$ generates the torsion field after adjoining that zero. We give an explicit $q$-linear formula recovering a torsion generator from this value. We also specialize the evaluation theorem of Gazda--Maurischat and compute the different as the principal ideal $(\partial_xp)$.

papers.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant \Gamma_{1,4} = 8
papers.abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants \Gamma_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Vector Valued Katok-Sarnak Formulas
papers.abstract: We introduce a version of the Katok-Sarnak formula linking twisted traces of scalar valued Maass cusp forms for $\Gamma_0(N)$ with $N$ square-free to Fourier coefficients of vector valued Maass cusp forms for the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and the Weil representation associated to a lattice of signature $(2,1)$. We prove this by computing the Fourier coefficients of the vector valued Siegel and Millson theta lift of a scalar valued newform by two different methods and comparing the results.

papers.title: Kloosterman Sums and Pl\"ucker Height Zeta Functions
papers.abstract: We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.

papers.title: Primes and the M\"obius function over quadratic polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for the number of primes $p\leq X$ of the form $n^2+h$ for almost all $h \leq X^{1/2-o(1)}$. We prove that, for almost all $h \leq X^{2/5}$, the number of primes satisfies a correct-order lower bound. We also show cancellation of the M\"obius function over $n^2+h$ for almost all $h < X^{1/2-o(1)}$.

papers.title: Twisted second moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions with applications to weighted one-level density
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.

papers.title: Irrationality of values of $L$-functions for real Dirichlet characters
papers.abstract: Let $\chi$ be a non-trivial real Dirichlet character and $s$ be a sufficiently large integer. In this paper, we prove that among the first $s$ non-critical special values of the Dirichlet $L$-function associated with $\chi$ at least $c\sqrt{\frac{s}{\log s}}$ are irrational, where $c$ is a constant independent of $s$. This is a substantial improvement on work of Fischler when $4$ divides the conductor of $\chi$. Otherwise, our constant improves on work of Mistiaen. The proof adapts some techniques of Lai and Yu for odd zeta values to the case of $L$-functions. The lack of positivity arguments is overcome by applying an irrationality criterion by Lai and Sprang originating from the $p$-adic setting.

papers.title: On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
papers.abstract: Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. These results were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
papers.abstract: We prove that the shifts $\zeta(s+id_j\tau)$, $1\le j\le n$, are jointly universal for any nonzero real parameters $d_j$ with pairwise distinct absolute values. These restrictions are best possible. As an immediate consequence, we obtain generalized strong recurrence for arbitrary finite families of nonzero real parameters. Our proof uses Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem and a new variant of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem.

papers.title: Estimates of Lucas series and expansions in non-integer bases
papers.abstract: Special Fibonacci and Lucas type expansions proved useful to ``correct'' some theorems on the number of expansions in non-integer bases \cite{BaiKomLor2021, KomLorPed2024, KomLorPed2025}. The proof of a key lemma was non-constructive. It was made constructive in the Fibonacci case by giving a precise estimate of the growth of the partial sums of the series of the inverses of the Fibonacci numbers \cite{KomPed2025}. In this paper we extend this result to the general case.

papers.title: On the modularity of residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2
papers.abstract: We use a new version of the Taylor--Wiles method, based on a tame analogue of the techniques introduced by Skinner--Wiles, to prove new modularity theorems for residually reducible Galois representations of rank 2 over totally real fields.

papers.title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

papers.title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
papers.abstract: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n \rho(n)e^{2\pi i n x}/n^s$, where $\rho(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $\phi$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $\Gamma\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $\Gamma$. Ordering the orbit $\Gamma\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\in\Gamma\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $\phi$. Previously this was known either when $\Gamma=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $\phi$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form. This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}\chi(n)e^{2\pi i n^2 x}/n^s$.

papers.title: On the Iwasawa invariants of admissible quadratic twists of elliptic curves at ordinary Eisenstein primes
papers.abstract: We study the Iwasawa $\mu$- and $\lambda$-invariants of quadratic twists of rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes $p\geq 3$. We verify Greenberg's $\mu=0$ conjecture for all such twists, which gives an Euler system free proof of Mazur's cotorsion conjecture, and study the $\lambda$-invariants when the twist is admissible in the sense of [GV00]. As a consequence, we prove the cyclotomic Iwasawa Main Conjecture and obtain the $p$-part BSD formulae in rank $0$ for admissible twists under mild conditions, covering many elliptic curves of potentially ordinary reduction.

papers.title: Descent and Decomposability of Algebras of Exponent 2 in characteristic 2
papers.abstract: We define an invariant of central simple algebras of degree 8 and exponent 2 over fields of characteristic 2. It is built from the discriminant Pfister forms of symplectic involutions, takes values in a quotient of the third part of the graded group associated to the fundamental filtration of the Witt group of quadratic forms, and vanishes on tensor products of three quaternion algebras, thus giving a necessary condition for decomposability. Variants of the consctuction yield necessary and sufficient conditions for a biquaternion algebra to descend from a quadratic extension of the base field, and for a quaternion algebra to descent from a biquadratic extension that is not purely inseparable. Our results extend known results both in characteristic 2 and in characteristic different from 2, see the introduction. Using residue maps for quadratic forms, we show that these invariants do not vanish in general, and we give an explicit central simple algebra of degree 8 and exponent 2 with nonzero invariant, which is therefore indecomposable. As explained in the appendix, the purely inseparable case is quite different; in particular, a quaternion algebra descents if and only if its Brauer class also does.

papers.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.

papers.title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $\phi$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $\rho$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_\rho$, $\overline{\Delta}_\rho$, $IC_\rho$, and $\delta_\rho$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$, which were conjectured to exist by Hansen. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp!}\pi$, and $i_{b!*}\pi$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $\pi$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $\phi$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus, as conjectured by Hansen and Hamann-Lee. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.
